name: Forró
notes: Forró style pack (Doc 04 template, solo-first). The Brazilian Northeast's dance: born in the sertão, carried to the nation by Luiz Gonzaga — the King of Baião — with the classic trio of zabumba (bass drum), triangle, and sanfona (accordion). Three rhythms shape a forró night: baião, xote (slower), and arrasta-pé (faster). Design truths: forró is one of the most beginner-friendly partner dances on earth — the base is a two-step anyone can walk into at a party — so the solo curriculum is compact and honest (the two-step, the xote step, weight-transfer quality, the zabumba ear), and the pack pushes you toward a real forró night early. Roots branches named honestly: pé-de-serra is the traditional root; universitário and eletrônico are later branches. Partner nodes flagged 🤝 and late-phase.

seasons.finale: Film yourself stepping the zabumba pattern through one full Gonzaga-style track — the ear leads the feet.
Film the forró basic — dois pra lá, dois pra cá — smooth for a full song, weight fully trading.
Film the xote step to a slow track — unhurried, grounded, swaying honest.
Frame prep done, basics automatic — find the forró night or class near you (there are more than you think).
Go dance forró with people. It's the friendliest floor in Brazil — the two-step you already own is the whole ticket in.

attributes.name: Zabumba ear L1
attributes.test: clap the zabumba's low beat through one full forró track without losing it

attributes.name: Weight transfer L1
attributes.test: 20 side-to-side transfers, weight fully arriving each time, knees soft, upper body calm

nodes.name: Baião — the zabumba's pattern
checkpoints: the zabumba plays low-boom then a dry slap — the baião cell your feet ride
the triangle keeps constant eighths on top; the sanfona (accordion) sings the story
find the low boom first: that's your 1

nodes.name: The three rhythms of a forró night
checkpoints: baião: the standard pulse — your two-step home
xote: slower and swaying — the close conversation
arrasta-pé: fast and stomping, feet dragging the floor — June festival (São João) energy

nodes.name: Luiz Gonzaga and the Northeast
checkpoints: forró comes from Brazil's Northeast — the sertão's parties, June festivals, and migrant halls
Luiz Gonzaga, the King of Baião, carried the sound to all of Brazil in the 1940s-50s — 'Asa Branca' is its anthem; know it
the classic trio is zabumba, triangle, and sanfona — three instruments, a whole party

nodes.name: Pé-de-serra and the branches
checkpoints: forró pé-de-serra is the traditional root — trio instruments, close hold, simple honest steps
universitário (1990s+) added turns and flourishes; eletrônico added pop production — branches, and they know it
start from the root: if your two-step works at a pé-de-serra party, everything else is decoration

nodes.name: The forró two-step (dois pra lá, dois pra cá)
nodes.anchor: learnable in one evening — that's the point of forró
checkpoints: two steps left, two steps right — weight fully trading, knees soft
small steps, grounded; forró is danced close, so the basic barely travels
sway comes from the transfer, not the shoulders
keep it going while holding a conversation — that's forró-ready
mistakes: steps so big a partner couldn't stay with you

nodes.name: The xote step
checkpoints: slower side-touch pattern with a gentle sway — the xote breathes
pauses are welcome; the slow songs are for settling, not filling
half-tempo control: the slower the song, the more honest the transfer must be
mistakes: rushing a slow song with busy feet

nodes.name: Arrasta-pé (the fast one)
checkpoints: same two-step, faster and lower — feet dragging the floor like the name says
São João festival energy: stomp, drag, grin
stamina check: one fast track without the step shrinking into a shuffle

nodes.name: Close-hold frame prep (solo)
checkpoints: forró is danced close: tall relaxed posture, arms carrying their own weight
practice the two-step with a light wall-touch — steady frame over moving feet
connection in forró is friendly and unforced; the frame just says 'I've got my own balance'

nodes.name: The close hold (with a partner)
checkpoints: learned at a forró night or class — famously the easiest partner floor to walk onto
the two-step you already own IS the dance; the hold just shares it
ask, connect kindly, and let the zabumba drive

nodes.name: Three rhythms, one film
checkpoints: film 30 seconds each: baião two-step, xote, arrasta-pé — name each on camera
the differences should be visible with the sound off
bonus: play 'Asa Branca' for the xote and mean it

nodes.name: The forró night
checkpoints: forró scenes exist far beyond Brazil — find the night or class nearest you and go
dance with people or just soak in the trio; both count
notice how fast strangers become dance partners here — that's the Northeast's gift
